sources.title: Zhang et al. 2014 — Crystal structure of human HSP70 substrate-binding domain with peptide substrate
sources.supports: Primary human HSP70 structure: two-layer beta-sandwich substrate pocket and alpha-helical lid; substrate binding is stronger in ADP state and weaker following ATP exchange. Schematic domain shapes are not fitted atomic coordinates.

sources.title: Allostery in the Hsp70 chaperones is transduced by subdomain rotations
sources.supports: Primary NMR evidence for nucleotide-dependent changes in NBD subdomains; ATP versus ADP affects domain coupling and client release. Supports the generic cycle, not exact model kinetics.

sources.title: EMBL-EBI — Alpha helix
sources.supports: Official structural teaching reference explicitly distinguishes helical handedness and gives right-handed alpha helix as the standard L-amino-acid protein conformation. It does not assert that rare left-handed conformations never exist.

findings.evidence: Final helix uses x increasing with y=+sin(theta), z=+cos(theta), giving left-handed chirality. Actual beads 0-22 at p=1/complete produce 20/20 negative consecutive-edge scalar triples, approximately -0.0031778853. All three manual Hsp70 lid helices likewise give 34/34 negative triples each, approximately -0.0001016377. The shared helix helper uses the opposite, right-handed convention.
findings.whyWrong: The model teaches a normal alpha/beta protein fold and an Hsp70 alpha-helical lid but constructs these representative alpha helices with reversed handedness. Rare left-handed protein conformations do not justify making the generic client and all lid helices left-handed without any such biological scope.
findings.fix: Reverse the manual angular orientation or use the right-handed helper while preserving coil endpoints, chain continuity, client-release choreography, shape detail and both branches.
findings.verification: Add actual-path chirality regressions for the final client helix and all three Hsp70 lid helices with a known right-handed positive control; ensure endpoints remain connected and all root/control cases pass.

continuity.checked: All update intervals, 468 independent frames and 1206 existing frames across three roots/two branches; arbitrary seeks deterministic; chain links stay connected.
findings: Handedness error persists in terminal complete branch and in lid geometry throughout both branches.
limits: Smooth positional interpolation alone is not validation of realistic molecular folding kinetics.
Client/chaperone contact is an enlarged schematic, not atomically fitted docking.

sources.supports: Primary SMN minigene/transcript evidence for exon 7 skipping and impaired SMNDelta7 self-association; supports inclusion versus skipping scope and avoids equating RNA variety with normal protein function.

sources.title: Galej et al. 2016 — Cryo-EM structure of the spliceosome immediately after branching
sources.supports: Primary 3.8 A spliceosome structure: first transesterification joins intron 5-prime phosphate to branch adenosine 2-prime OH; cleaved 5-prime exon is retained near the catalytic site. Splicing proceeds through branching followed by exon ligation.

findings.kind: misleading reaction geometry and visible bond pop
findings.evidence: New exon-ligation bonds become fully visible at p=.59 while exon approach is still in progress (.55-.73). Actual skip endpoints are 4.4068587 units apart and inclusion endpoints are 1.4980796 apart; ordinary RNA backbone spacing is .1. These giant bonds immediately appear then contract to .3/.1. First transesterification has the same order problem: at p=.349 its new branch bond spans 2.23371 units (skip) or .71457 (include).
findings.whyWrong: Transesterification is drawn as creating a long covalent tether across remote RNA segments instead of first bringing reactive endpoints together at the spliceosomal active site. The model itself presents these cylinders as RNA bonds; their conspicuous appearance across a substantial part of the scene cannot be treated as a harmless length-scale label.
findings.fix: Choreograph RNA approach and bending before either bond exchange; switch donor/branch and acceptor/new-exon connectivity only when respective endpoints are adjacent. After ligation move the connected product without stretching its new junction, retaining original nucleotide identities and both lariat outcomes.
findings.verification: Regression must inspect actual branch/exon bond endpoints and lengths at both reaction instants, throughout intermediate progress and in both isoforms; reject the baseline long-link spans; preserve branched RNA and retained/excised exon identity.

continuity.checked: 156 independent frames and 402 existing frames; detailed switches .34/.348/.59/.73 plus source-derived thresholds.
findings: 20261004-translation-03: long covalent cylinders pop into view and subsequently contract.
limits: The mere presence of an instantaneous bond exchange is appropriate; defect is the demonstrably remote reaction geometry.
Spliceosome later visibility removal is a schematic turnover boundary; no extra defect assigned solely for that switch.

sources.title: RCSB 3U7Q — A. vinelandii nitrogenase MoFe protein at atomic resolution
sources.supports: Primary 1.00 A MoFe structure from A. vinelandii; central light atom in FeMo cofactor identified as carbon. Model cluster schematic retains distinct composition and alpha-domain placement.

findings.evidence: N2 is visible while p<.81, whereas both separate NH3 groups become visible at p>=.8. Actual nitrogen-sphere count is 2 at .799999, 4 at .8/.805/.809999, and 2 at .81. The overlap lasts .36 s at the declared 36 s duration, with opaque materials and fully present product nitrogen spheres.
findings.whyWrong: One represented N2 substrate is converted to two NH3 products, so it cannot coexist with an extra pair of product nitrogen atoms during that same conversion. This is duplicated molecular matter, not merely teaching-marker stoichiometry.
findings.fix: Transfer the two existing nitrogen identities into the product representation at a single coherent conversion boundary, or make substrate/product visibility mutually exclusive and align product starting positions to the same atoms; preserve two NH3 and H2, all eight rounds and the blocked branch.
findings.verification: Assert exactly two effective visible nitrogen atom representations in the active substrate-to-product trajectory at dense boundary samples; assert no product in exposed branch. Root should inspect continuity at .78-.83.
